source_text:
Μὴ κάμῃς ἀνόνητα, μὴ εἰς ἀσέβειαν ἀναλώσῃς τὰ σά, μὴ κατὰ θεοῦ φαντάζου τὴν νίκην, μὴ δῷς μισθὸν στρατιώταις
ἕτερα ἀνθ' ἑτέρων εἰπεῖν, μὴ παρακοιμίσῃς τὸν ὄχλον τῷ μνήματι, μὴ θαρρήσῃς τοῖς ὅπλοις. Ὅπλοις ἀνάστασις οὐ κωλύεται, οὐκ ἐμποδίζεται ταῖς σφραγίσιν, οὐκ εἴργεται στρατιώταις, οὐ κλέπτεται χρήμασιν. Ἀλλ' ἀπιστεῖς; Μὴ οὐκ εἶδες τὸν Λάζαρον πάλαι καθάπερ ὕπνον τὸν θάνατον ἀποσεισάμενον; Εἶδες πῶς ἠκολούθησε τῷ προστάγματι ὁ νεκρὸς καὶ ὁ δεσμὸς οὐκ ἐκώλυσε; Εἶδες πῶς σὺν αὐταῖς κηρίαις ἐβάδιζε τὸ ∆εῦρο ἔξω ἀκούσας; Εἶδες πῶς ἥρμοσεν ἡ φωνὴ τὸν διαλυθέντα θανάτῳ; Ὁ ἐκεῖνα δυνηθεὶς καὶ ταῦτα δυνήσεται, ὁ τὸν δοῦλον ἀναστήσας αὐτὸς πολλῷ πλέον ἐγείρεται, ὁ ζωογονήσας τὸν σεσηπότα οὐκ ἐάσει νεκρὸν ἑαυτόν. Ἀλλὰ γὰρ ἡ τυφλότης τῶν Ἰουδαίων πολλὴ καὶ ὁρῶσα τὰ θαύματα οὐχ ὁρᾷ· ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχουσιν καὶ οὐ βλέπουσιν, ὦτα ἔχουσι καὶ οὐκ ἀκούουσιν. Ὁ θεὸς γὰρ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου ἐτύφλωσε αὐτῶν τὰς καρδίας πρὸς τὸ μὴ καταυγάσαι αὐτοῖς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς δικαιοσύνης. Ἀλλ' ἐκείνους μὲν τέως ἐάσωμεν τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ, ἡμεῖς δὲ λέγωμεν μετὰ τῶν περὶ Μαριὰν τὴν πιστὴν κατὰ διάνοιαν ἀναπλάττοντες ἑαυτοῖς τοῦ σωτῆρος τὸν τάφον· Ἦραν ἡμῶν τὸν κύριον καὶ οὐκ οἴδαμεν τί ἐποίησαν αὐτόν. Αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα σὺν τῷ ἀχράντῳ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι, νῦν καὶ ἀεί, καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν. 2
thought_title: The tomb cannot hold the risen Lord
orientation: The preacher is addressing the Jew who sealed and guarded the tomb, challenging him to stop fighting God and to remember the raising of Lazarus as proof that Christ will rise.
pass_a_gloss: Do not labour [to] no profit, do not spend your own [resources] on impiety, do not imagine victory against God, do not give pay to soldiers to say other [things] instead of other [things], do not make the crowd sleep beside the tomb, do not trust in weapons. By weapons resurrection is not hindered, [it] is not impeded by seals, [it] is not barred by soldiers, [it] is not stolen by money. But do you disbelieve? Did you not see Lazarus long ago shaking off death just as sleep? Did you see how the corpse obeyed the command and the binding did not hinder? Did you see how with the very grave-cloths he walked, having heard the 'Come out'? Did you see how the voice fitted together the [one] dissolved by death? The [one] able [to do] those [things] will be able [to do] these [things] also; the [one] who raised the servant will himself be raised much more; the [one] who made alive the [one] already decayed will not leave himself dead. But indeed the blindness of the Jews [is] great, and seeing the wonders [it] does not see; eyes they have and they do not see, ears they have and they do not hear. For the god of this age blinded their hearts so that the gospel of righteousness should not shine upon them. But let us leave those [ones] for now in unbelief, but let us say with those around Mary, faithfully shaping for ourselves in thought the tomb of the Saviour: 'They took away our Lord and we do not know what they did [with] him.' To him [be] the glory with the undefiled Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always, and to the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.why: The adverb conveys futile effort; 'to no profit' keeps the sense of wasted labour without adding a moralising gloss.
The verb means to picture or imagine in the mind; 'imagine victory' preserves the delusional quality of the Jew's hope.

choices.english: make the crowd sleep beside the tomb
choices.why: The compound verb means to make someone sleep beside something; the rendering keeps the physical proximity to the tomb, which is the point of the guard.
rejected: lull the crowd to sleep at the tomb
put the crowd to bed by the tomb

choices.term: ἥρμοσεν ἡ φωνὴ τὸν διαλυθέντα θανάτῳ
choices.english: the voice fitted together the one dissolved by death
choices.why: The verb means to join or fit together; 'fitted together' conveys the restoration of the decomposed body by the command.
The glossary requires 'unbelief' for ἀπιστία; the dative is rendered as a state in which they are left.

choices.term: ἀναπλάττοντες ἑαυτοῖς τοῦ σωτῆρος τὸν τάφον
choices.english: shaping for ourselves in thought the tomb of the Saviour
choices.why: The participle means to mould or form in the mind; 'shaping for ourselves in thought' captures the imaginative act of picturing the tomb.
rejected: forming in our minds the tomb

bible_refs.note: ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχουσιν καὶ οὐ βλέπουσιν, ὦτα ἔχουσι καὶ οὐκ ἀκούουσιν
ὁ θεὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου ἐτύφλωσε αὐτῶν τὰς καρδίας
Ἦραν ἡμῶν τὸν κύριον καὶ οὐκ οἴδαμεν τί ἐποίησαν αὐτόν (adapted to plural)

pass_b_english: Do not labour to no profit. Do not spend what is yours on impiety. Do not imagine victory against God. Do not pay soldiers to say one thing instead of another. Do not make the crowd sleep beside the tomb. Do not trust in weapons. Resurrection is not hindered by weapons, is not blocked by seals, is not barred by soldiers, is not stolen with money. But do you not believe? Did you not see Lazarus long ago shaking off death as if it were sleep? Did you see how the dead man obeyed the command and the binding did not hinder him? Did you see how he walked with his grave-cloths still on when he heard "Come out" (John 11:43)? Did you see how the voice fitted together the one dissolved by death? The one who had power for those things will have power for these things too. The one who raised the servant will himself rise far more. The one who gave life to the rotting man will not leave himself dead. But the blindness of the Jews is great, and seeing the wonders they do not see. They have eyes but do not see, ears have they and do not hear (Isaiah 6:9-10). For the god of this age has blinded their hearts so that the gospel of righteousness may not shine upon them (2 Corinthians 4:4). But let us leave them for now in unbelief, and let us say with the women around Mary, shaping for ourselves in thought the tomb of the Saviour: "They have taken away our Lord and we do not know what they have done with him" (John 20:2). To him be glory with the undefiled Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always, and to the ages of ages. Amen.

last_rejected.quote: Do not labour to no profit. Do not spend what is yours on impiety. Do not imagine victory against God. Do not pay soldiers to say one thing instead of another. Do not make the crowd sleep beside the tomb. Do not trust in weapons.
last_rejected.source_quote: Μὴ κάμῃς ἀνόνητα, μὴ εἰς ἀσέβειαν ἀναλώσῃς τά σά, μὴ κατὰ θεοῦ φαντάζου τὴν νίκην, μὴ δῷς μισθὸν στρατιώταις ἕτερα ἀνθ' ἑτέρων εἰπεῖν, μὴ παρακοιμίσῃς τὸν ὄχλον τῷ μνήματι, μὴ θαρρήσῃς τοῖς ὅπλοις
last_rejected.why: English hides that this is the preacher addressing the Jew in second person singular; 'Do not' could be generic.
last_rejected.fix: Do not you labour to no profit. Do not you spend what is yours on impiety.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek uses 2nd‑person singular imperative; English imperative likewise addresses the listener.

last_rejected.quote: Do not make the crowd sleep beside the tomb
last_rejected.source_quote: μὴ παρακοιμίσῃς τὸν ὄχλον τῷ μνήματι
last_rejected.why: παρακοιμίσῃς means 'post beside, station as guards', not 'make sleep'; the guards were posted, not lulled to sleep.
last_rejected.fix: Do not post the crowd beside the tomb
last_rejected.ruling: παρακοιμίσῃς derives from κοιμάω ‘to put to sleep’; translation matches meaning.

last_rejected.quote: Do not pay soldiers to say one thing instead of another
last_rejected.source_quote: μὴ δῷς μισθὸν στρατιώταις ἕτερα ἀνθ' ἑτέρων εἰπεῖν
last_rejected.why: ἕτερα ἀνθ' ἑτέρων means 'one thing for another' i.e. 'to change their story, lie', not merely 'say one thing instead of another'.
last_rejected.fix: Do not pay soldiers to change their story
last_rejected.ruling: Greek phrase means bribe soldiers to speak differently; English conveys that idea adequately.

last_rejected.quote: the voice fitted together the one dissolved by death
last_rejected.source_quote: ἥρμοσεν ἡ φωνὴ τὸν διαλυθέντα θανάτῳ
last_rejected.why: ἥρμοσεν here means 'fitted together, reassembled, restored'—the voice put back together what death had dissolved.
last_rejected.fix: the voice reassembled the one dissolved by death
last_rejected.ruling: ἥρμοσεν = ‘fit together’; translation reflects same sense.
